site.name: Proud Partners
site.description: Proud Partners brings people, knowledge and practical support together to strengthen communities in the Western Cape.

home.title: Partnership changes what is possible.
home.intro: Proud Partners is run by South Africans who believe meaningful change begins when people share their time, knowledge and expertise. We connect individuals and organisations around practical projects that make daily life better.
home.featureTitle: A brighter future is something we build together.
home.featureCopy: From classrooms and music programmes to child care and community initiatives, every project starts with listening and grows through long-term relationships.
home.missionQuote: When people notice the needs of others, have empathy and do something about it, a country changes.
home.videoTitle: What do you want to become?
home.videoCopy: A place is ready for the children’s video. Add its YouTube or Vimeo embed URL here when the original file or link is available.

about.title: A story of partnership
about.lead: Proud Partners was established in 2004 after the founding partners visited Khayelitsha in the Western Cape. Moved by the reality of the living conditions—and by the optimism and goodwill they encountered—they decided to become directly involved.
about.photoCaption: Dr Prieur du Plessis and Proud Partners founder Isabel Verwey.
about.originTitle: The partnership that started it all
origin: When Isabel Verwey moved to Cape Town in 1994, her domestic worker of thirteen years, Selina, moved with her. Years later, Selina presented Isabel with a certificate that read: “In recognition of 20 years of partnership.”

What first sounded like an unusual word for their relationship captured it exactly: they were partners in work and in life, sharing concern for their families, exchanging advice and looking out for one another. That spirit became the heart of Proud Partners.

principles.title: Brief history
principles.copy: With early financial support from Plexus Asset Management, Proud Partners grew from one local project into a network of education, arts, care and community initiatives.

principles.title: Mission
principles.copy: To encourage South Africans to identify a partner with whom they can walk through life—sharing practical help, knowledge and opportunity across communities.

principles.title: How we work
principles.copy: Proud Partners is built on cooperation rather than once-off charity. Projects ask for time, energy and commitment from everyone involved, with the goal of lasting benefit and mutual understanding.

support.title: Stand beside a project
support.copy: Proud Partners does not use a general online donation or contact form. You can learn more, enquire or contribute through the organisations currently featured below.

home.mastheadCaption: One country. Many lives. Shared responsibility.
home.portraitNote: A fresh focus on the people at the heart of the work.
home.projectsCopy: Each initiative is different, but the method stays the same: bring the right people together and make practical progress.

about.seoDescription: Learn how Proud Partners began and why partnership, practical assistance and mutual understanding guide its work.
about.methodStatement: Not help from a distance. A commitment to walk alongside one another.

projects.seoDescription: Explore Proud Partners projects across education, music, child care, art and community partnership.
projects.title: Bright ideas become shared action.
projects.intro: Proud Partners began with one project in 2004. It grew through relationships—one practical idea, one committed partner and one community at a time.
projects.listCopy: The Nianell motivational programme now forms part of Educational Projects, bringing its message of confidence and possibility into the wider learning programme.

projects.title: Educational projects
projects.summary: Opening doors through early learning, school partnerships, reading, mathematics and motivational programmes.
projects.imageAlt: An educator working with children in a classroom
body: Education is one of the clearest ways to narrow the gap between very different everyday realities. Proud Partners supports projects that help learners discover their ability, build confidence and access opportunity.
The Nianell Motivational Project now sits within this education programme, where its message of possibility belongs.

initiatives.title: School and reading partnerships
initiatives.copy: Long-term partnerships have included early childhood development, reading support and practical assistance to schools in communities with limited resources.

initiatives.title: Mathematics support
initiatives.copy: Focused academic projects give senior learners extra tools, time and guidance in subjects that can unlock further study.

initiatives.title: Nianell motivational programme
initiatives.copy: Singer and honorary Proud Partners member Nianell used music and motivational talks to encourage learners to recognise their potential and imagine a bigger future.

projects.title: Music projects
projects.summary: Making instruments, tuition and performance opportunities available to young South Africans.
body: Music breaks down barriers between people and cultures. Training does more than teach technique: it builds discipline, expression, belonging and confidence.
Proud Partners has supported school music programmes, young musicians, choirs and the donation of instruments.

initiatives.title: Durbanville Children’s Home
initiatives.copy: With support from Global Music and Yamaha, Proud Partners donated recorders and a keyboard to help music become part of the healing and development of children in care.

initiatives.title: Tygerberg Children’s Choir
initiatives.copy: Proud Partners helped talented young choristers participate fully in a world-class musical community and supported choir fees for children who needed assistance.

initiatives.title: Young musicians
initiatives.copy: Individual support has included instruments and opportunities for promising learners whose commitment outpaced their available resources.

projects.title: PJO Inni Bosch
projects.summary: A public art initiative that invited young artists and the wider Stellenbosch community to create together.
projects.imageAlt: A group of children gathered together outdoors
body: Through the PJO Art Centre in Stellenbosch, Proud Partners launched a street art competition designed to change the face of the town and give emerging artists a public platform.
The project brought art into everyday spaces, with prizes for both artists and members of the public.

initiatives.title: Art in public
initiatives.copy: A creative town-wide experience encouraged people to follow the work as it unfolded and to see familiar places differently.

projects.title: Child care projects
projects.summary: Supporting capable organisations that provide specialist care to children and their families.
body: Many children from disadvantaged backgrounds struggle to access the care they need. Proud Partners has chosen to stand alongside organisations already doing skilled, compassionate work.
This approach keeps support close to the people who understand the families, the context and the long-term needs.

initiatives.title: Iris House Children’s Hospice
initiatives.copy: Iris House provides free community- and hospice-based respite care, therapies and whole-family support to children and young people with life-limiting or life-threatening conditions.

initiatives.title: Specialist partners
initiatives.copy: Past projects have also highlighted children’s hospices, medical charities and local fundraising initiatives whose expertise creates meaningful care.

projects.title: Domestic partnership
projects.summary: Practical knowledge and mutual care for the women who work and live alongside one another.
projects.imageAlt: A woman standing outdoors with household tools
body: The relationship between South African women and the domestic workers in their homes was the original inspiration for Proud Partners.
The project focuses on seeing one another fully and sharing useful knowledge, advice and support in ways that strengthen both households.

initiatives.title: Knowledge shared
initiatives.copy: Practical conversations can cover family wellbeing, education, financial choices and access to resources—small interventions that can have lasting value.

initiatives.title: Partnership over charity
initiatives.copy: The guiding idea is reciprocal concern: people who work together can also look out for one another and learn from one another.

projects.title: Plexus charity walk
projects.summary: A team challenge in Ceres that turned kilometres walked into meaningful project funding.
projects.imageAlt: Children gathered around desks and a chalkboard outdoors
body: In 2005, Plexus staff and their families walked in Ceres for two days with an ambitious collective target of 1,000 kilometres.
Through sponsorships, the event raised R80,000 for Proud Partners projects and demonstrated how a workplace community could turn participation into practical support.

initiatives.title: A founding partnership
initiatives.copy: Plexus Asset Management provided early financial support when Proud Partners was established and continued that spirit through a hands-on fundraising challenge.

consularBall.seoDescription: The story and impact of the Cape Town Consular Ball, bringing international representatives and local partners together for young people.
consularBall.title: The Consular Ball
consularBall.intro: An annual gathering where international representatives, local business leaders and community organisations turn one remarkable evening into practical support for young people.
consularBall.originTitle: One room. More than fifty nations. A shared purpose.
origin: Isabel Verwey became involved in the Cape Town Consular Corps when her husband, Dr Prieur du Plessis, was appointed Honorary Consul of Slovenia in South Africa. Seeing the potential of the city’s consular community, she organised the first Consular Ball in 2012 in aid of local charities, including Proud Partners.

The event grew into a highlight of Cape Town’s social calendar. Consular missions invite businesspeople with South African interests, while leaders from the city, local government and the Western Cape business community gather around a carefully selected group of causes.
consularBall.yearsCopy: Select a year to explore the milestones. The archive combines the surviving Proud Partners photographs with the published fundraising history.
consularBall.auctionCopy: The Ball became known for an unconventional auction of unique experiences: tea with Archbishop Desmond Tutu, a customised journey to Antarctica, and an intimate dinner with Gift of the Givers founder Dr Imtiaz Sooliman were among the standout lots.
consularBall.closingQuote: The power of the states represented in the Mother City can make a meaningful contribution to social justice and community development.

externalLink.label: Visit the Cape Town Consular Corps

years.title: The first Ball
years.summary: Isabel organised the inaugural Consular Ball in aid of local charities. The evening established the model: diplomatic missions, business leaders and community causes in one room.
years.imageAlt: Champagne glasses prepared for the first Consular Ball

years.title: A tradition takes shape
years.summary: The second Ball built on the first year’s momentum as more consular missions and members of Cape Town’s business community joined the initiative.
years.imageAlt: A formal place setting and auction booklet at the Consular Ball
highlights: The charity auction became a defining feature

years.title: Partnership gathers momentum
years.summary: By its third year, the Ball had established a distinctive international character and a growing reputation for connecting generous guests with practical local causes.
years.imageAlt: An illuminated floral centrepiece at the Consular Ball

years.title: A major step forward
years.summary: The Consular Ball went from strength to strength, raising an impressive R800,000 for its selected charities.
years.imageAlt: A Swiss-themed table at the Consular Ball
highlights: A landmark year for the event

years.title: Sustained impact
years.summary: The 2016 Ball continued the event’s strong fundraising record, contributing R700,000 to organisations working with young people.
years.imageAlt: An elegant dinner setting at the Consular Ball
highlights: Continued focus on youth and community causes

years.title: A record-breaking evening
years.summary: The event reached a new record of R950,000. The Tygerberg Children’s Choir also gave a moving performance to guests from more than twenty countries.
years.imageAlt: A chandelier and floral display at the 2017 Consular Ball

years.title: Breaking the million-rand mark
years.summary: The Ball passed the R1 million fundraising benchmark for the first time, confirming its place as an important platform for collective giving in Cape Town.
years.imageAlt: The formal ballroom prepared for the 2018 Consular Ball

years.title: A remarkable return
years.summary: After a three-year interruption during the coronavirus pandemic, the Consular Ball returned and shattered its previous record with R1.8 million raised.
years.imageAlt: An international table setting at the returning Consular Ball

partnersPage.seoDescription: Meet the donors, organisations, artists and community specialists who make Proud Partners projects possible.
partnersPage.title: Our partners
partnersPage.intro: Proud Partners works because people and organisations contribute what they do best—funding, specialist care, instruments, expertise, creativity and time.
partnersPage.sectionCopy: Core donors make long-term work possible; project partners bring specialist knowledge and direct community relationships. Every contribution is part of the same shared effort.
partnersPage.closingCopy: The aim is not help from a distance, but useful relationships built on listening, trust and shared responsibility.
